PROTEST. Militants gather at Liwasang Bonifacio in Manila on November 15, 2026, to protest the proposed Pax Silica initiative and US President Donald Trump’s visit to the 49th ASEAN Summit.
MANILA, Philippines – US President Donald Trump ’s arrival in Manila on Tuesday, November 17, is expected to draw protests, with activists preparing to march against the US-led Pax Silica.
Protesters have been holding a campout at Liwasang Bonifacio since Sunday, November 15. They plan to march to the Philippine International Convention Center, the venue of the ASEAN-US Special Summit which Trump will attend, ahead of the US leader’s arrival.
The protesters are opposing Pax Silica, a US-led initiative that seeks to secure supply chains for critical minerals and semiconductors through partnerships with other countries.
Trump is expected to arrive in the Philippines at 5:30 pm. He will conduct a state visit before leaving the country on Wednesday, November 18.
On Wednesday, when Trump will be in Malacañang for activities related to his state visit, protesters are expected to converge in Liwasang Bonifacio and march to Mendiola, near Malacañang.
Roads leading to Ayala Bridge and Recto Avenue toward Mendiola Peace Arch are closed to both motorists and pedestrians. Fences and barriers have been installed around the area.
Activists have warned that Pax Silica could put indigenous communities and farming areas at risk, particularly amid growing demand for minerals used in advanced technologies.
The Philippine National Police has deployed around 20,000 personnel across summit venues and nearby areas.
Security forces faced protesters on the summit’s opening day on Sunday, when police arrested around 300 people in Manila and Muntinlupa . The arrests drew condemnation from lawmakers and various groups. – Rappler.com
